scope: Static read-only review of versioned OOM recovery and checkpoint restore; no runtime/GPU/MCP/Drive access.
overall: Gradient-checkpointing path and state restore appear internally coherent, but migration binding should pin the exact source checkpoint and backend hash before calling it fail-closed.
verified: Worker config comparison preserves exact source plan, dev, contract, deadline, source view/manifest, policy, and optimizer parameter names; only explicit worker migration plus gradient_checkpointing false→true and loss-description text are allowed.

Checkpoint restore compares adapter tensors exactly, checks optimizer parameter-name mapping/coherence, restores optimizer and GradScaler state, then restores Torch CPU/CUDA and Python RNG states; cursor/training time come from checkpoint.
Log reconciliation verifies acknowledged prefix IDs/cursor/steps/token counts and hash, stores the unapplied tail immutably, then truncates working log to the committed prefix.

Backend requests PEFT k-bit preparation with use_reentrant=False; training mode enables checkpointing with the same setting and use_cache=False. No obvious frozen-base/LoRA gradient incompatibility in code; runtime progress confirms path initialized, though no external validation was done.

findings.issue: memory_resume_migration.json names the intended cp1 generation and manifest/archive hashes, but worker validation does not compare args.resume_generation.name or its manifest SHA to those fields. A different otherwise-compatible generation could inherit the v4→v5 exception.
findings.recommendation: Before loading checkpoint state, require exact parent_checkpoint_generation and parent_generation_manifest_sha256 match; bind archive SHA if the archive is the transfer artifact.

findings.issue: Migration JSON records resumed_backend_sha256, but worker does not verify it against native_backend_v3.py bytes. worker_sha pins the caller file only, not its imported backend implementation.
findings.recommendation: Verify the backend SHA against migration receipt/config immediately before import/use and persist it in run_config.

findings.issue: Allowlist admits `loss_reduction` text change as well as code/checkpointing. It is documented as a clarification only and code weighting is unchanged, but current check does not pin the old/new exact text.
findings.recommendation: Bind exact parent and resumed loss_reduction strings (or exclude this field from runtime diff by carrying the parent description plus separate correction note).

gradient_checkpointing_review.double_enable: prepare_model_for_kbit_training enables it and for_training enables again; likely idempotent but redundant. Remove duplicate enable only in a future version, not during this run.
gradient_checkpointing_review.optimizer_parameters: Gradient checkpointing does not itself alter trainable parameter names/order; exact name check protects optimizer-state mapping.
gradient_checkpointing_review.numerical_caveat: Recomputation can cause small FP16 numerical drift; migration preserves schedule/state but not bitwise identical trajectory.
